title: Best Bookkeeping software for Dutch holding companies
content_html:
The best bookkeeping software for Dutch holding companies depends on how many BVs (Dutch private limited companies) sit in the group and who does the books. Moneybird and e-Boekhouden fit an entrepreneur with one BV, Exact Online fits groups that also need ERP, and Bookwise from Upward Technologies is made for Dutch BV groups.

What is bookkeeping software for a Dutch holding company?

It is software that keeps the books for a group where a holding BV owns one or more other BVs. Each BV is its own company with its own administration. That means the owner or the accountant works across several sets of books, not one.

This matters because most bookkeeping packages start from one company. When a group grows to two, three or more BVs, the questions change. How do you switch between the BVs? How do you record invoices and payments between your own companies? How do you see the whole group at once?

Best bookkeeping software for Dutch holding companies: the main options

The table below uses what each vendor says about itself on its own website, read in November 2026. It does not describe prices or plans. Check those on each vendor's site.

OptionWhat its website says it isWho it tends to suit
Exact OnlineCloud accounting and ERP software for SMEs and accountantsGroups that also want ERP, CRM or HR in the same system
MoneybirdOne package for all financial matters, for anyone from a starting freelancer to a growing BVAn owner with one BV who wants to do the books themselves
e-BoekhoudenA Dutch online accounting program for entrepreneurs, accountants and associationsAn owner who wants a direct link to the tax office for VAT returns
Bookwise (Upward Technologies)Bookkeeping for Dutch BV groupsHolding groups with several BVs

Exact Online

Exact describes itself as a Dutch company that builds cloud-based accounting, ERP and business management software for SMEs and accountants. According to its website, Exact Online covers finance, ERP, CRM and HR. It includes AI agents for bank, purchase and debtor tasks as standard, and it gets monthly releases. Exact also offers separate tax and annual reporting editions and practice management tools for accounting firms.

Exact Online is a strong choice when the holding group also runs an operating company that needs stock, orders or HR in the same place as the books.

Moneybird

Moneybird describes itself as an accounting package that brings all of an entrepreneur's financial matters together. According to its website, it works out VAT (value added tax) from your invoices and receipts. It reads the amount, VAT and supplier from purchase invoices and books most of them itself. It can send invoices through the Peppol network (a network for sending e-invoices) and link a business account at almost any Dutch bank.

Moneybird is a good fit for an owner who runs one BV and wants simple, do-it-yourself bookkeeping.

e-Boekhouden

e-Boekhouden describes itself as a Dutch online accounting program for entrepreneurs, accountants and associations or foundations. According to its website, it has a direct link with the Belastingdienst (the Dutch tax office) for VAT returns. Its site states it is recognised by the Belastingdienst. It covers bookkeeping, invoicing, quotes, time tracking, customer management and stock, and it has an API (a connection other software can use) and a mobile app.

Its site also offers accounting firms one place to manage all their client administrations. If you have several BVs, ask e-Boekhouden whether that setup also works for an owner's own group.

Your accountant

Many holding companies hand the books to an accounting firm. That is often the right answer when the owner wants no part in the daily work. In that case, the best software is usually the one your accountant already works with. Ask them before you choose.

Bookwise

Bookwise is the bookkeeping product from Upward Technologies (upwardtech.nl). It is built for Dutch BV groups. It is a newer product than the packages above, so ask for a walkthrough and compare it against your own group before you switch.

How to choose

Start with your group, not with a feature list. These questions sort out most of the choice:

  • How many BVs are in the group? With one BV, a package made for single companies is often enough. With several, ask each vendor how you move between BVs and whether one login covers them all.
  • Do your BVs invoice or pay each other? Ask how the software records these transactions between your own companies on both sides.
  • Who does the work? If your accountant does the books, their choice of software carries a lot of weight.
  • What does it need to connect to? Think of your bank, the Belastingdienst, e-invoicing and any ERP or CRM in an operating BV. This guide on how to connect ERP and CRM so data is entered once covers that side.
  • Where is your data stored? Read each vendor's terms and processing agreement. Do not assume.
  • Do you need more than bookkeeping? If the group also needs ERP, CRM or HR, a broad suite such as Exact Online may save you from running separate tools.

If your group overview today lives in a spreadsheet that only one person understands, read when to replace a spreadsheet with custom software before you buy anything.

Where Upward Technologies fits

Upward Technologies is a small software company in Breda. For holding groups it offers Bookwise, its bookkeeping product for Dutch BV groups.

Plainly, Upward Technologies is not always the right choice:

  • One BV and you do your own books: Moneybird or e-Boekhouden is likely the simpler pick.
  • You also need ERP, CRM or HR in one system: Exact Online is built for that.
  • Your accountant does everything: use what your accountant uses.
  • Several BVs and you want software made for a group: look at Bookwise.

Some groups need more than a package. An operating BV may run its own systems that have to feed the books.
